item.title: Jorge Jesus breaks silence on Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal retirement
item.description: Jorge Jesus has insisted he bears no responsibility for Cristiano Ronaldo ’s decision to step away from international football. The 41-year-old forward called time on his Portugal career on Thursday, finishing with men's record totals of 234 caps and 146 goals. His announcement arrived under a month after receiving a backdated 30-day ban and a 255 euro (roughly £210) fine from the Portuguese Football Federation. The sanction was imposed after the forward walked out on the squad before a Nations League clash with Denmark on 1 October, following a disagreement with Jesus. With the suspension served, Ronaldo was eligible for selection for upcoming fixtures against Denmark and Wales. Unveiling his squad for those games on Friday, Jesus – who managed Ronaldo at Saudi club Al Nassr prior to taking the Portugal job in July – maintained he felt no guilt over the end of the five-time Ballon d’Or winner’s 23-year career on the international stage. Jesus said: "No, maybe I rushed things, but not because of me. It was in his head, more call-ups, fewer call-ups. "We also talked about it a few times. And if it was going to happen. But no, I don’t feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision. "And, as such, his story cannot be ignored. He will always be a symbol and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half. "Sporting-wise, he made a decision and I greatly respect his decision." Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday after 234 caps and 146 goals (Getty) The 72-year-old manager explained that he received no advance notice of Ronaldo’s retirement prior to its publication on social media, confirming he would have otherwise been named in the squad. "I found out when we all did," Jesus said. "Until then, I knew nothing about it. "He was playing, he was scoring goals; he was one of the players on my squad list." Ronaldo had alleged that Jesus had "broken his word" by keeping him on the bench throughout a match against Norway on 27 September. The forward spent time warming up during the second period in Oslo before remaining an unused substitute, subsequently departing the team camp. Responding to questions regarding the rift, Jesus said: "All my decisions were made with the team in mind. "As a manager, I have always defended what was best for the team. I am at peace with my decision." Jesus noted that he had not spoken with Ronaldo following Thursday’s statement. Offering a tribute to the departing forward, PFF president Pedro Proenca said: "No tribute will ever be enough to thank him for everything he has done for Portuguese football. "Thank you for everything, captain. This is and always will be your home."

item.title: Mbappe headlines Zidane's France squad, Pagis gets call-up
item.description: France coach Zinedine Zidane is all smiles as he speaks at a press conference in Paris on Friday (FRANCK FIFE) Kylian Mbappe headlined the France squad named Friday by coach Zinedine Zidane for their Nations League matches against Italy and Turkey after picking up an injury on international duty in September, while Pablo Pagis was handed a debut call-up. Real Madrid superstar Mbappe, the France captain, scored the winner in Zidane's first match in charge of Les Bleus away to Turkey on September 25, but suffered a knee injury in the same game that ruled him out of the team's three remaining fixtures of the last international window. Without him, France won twice against Belgium, in Brussels and then at home, and drew in between against Italy. Mbappe has since returned to action for his club, scoring eight times in seven matches between La Liga and the Champions League. France are without Paris Saint-Germain star Ousmane Dembele and Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul for this month's double-header, so Marcus Thuram of Inter Milan is recalled to an attack which will also feature Pagis for the first time. The 23-year-old Pagis, who plays chiefly as an attacking midfielder, is rewarded for his impressive form this season since joining Paris FC -- who are fourth in Ligue 1 -- from Lorient. Pagis is the son of Mickael Pagis, the former Marseille player who at one time appeared for the France beach soccer team coached by Eric Cantona. Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid returns in midfield in place of Manu Kone after missing the last international window, while Manchester United's Leny Yoro and Chelsea's Malo Gusto replace Jules Kounde of Barcelona and Maxence Lacroix of Chelsea in the defence. Zidane's side play Italy in Milan next Thursday, November 12, and then take on Turkey in Bordeaux three days later in their final group-stage fixtures. They are top of Nations League Group A1 with 10 points from four outings, three ahead of Italy. The top two teams in the group will advance to the quarter-finals next March. item.title: Jose Mourinho’s excellent record at Mestalla in focus ahead of Valencia vs Real Madrid
item.description: Jose Mourinho’s excellent record at Mestalla in focus ahead of Valencia vs Real Madrid Real Madrid will have an excellent opportunity to put more pressure on Barcelona at the top of the league table as they take on Valencia tomorrow. With the top two in Barcelona facing Atletico Madrid in the same weekend, Real Madrid will have an opportunity to get into an advantageous position by the end of this gameweek. However, scoring points away at Mestalla against Valencia is always a challenge for most teams across Europe, let alone only Spanish clubs. Mourinho’s record at Mestalla Mestalla, though, has been a stomping ground of sorts for Jose Mourinho throughout his career as manager. Mourinho has a picture perfect record at the Mestalla. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Indeed, the Portuguese tactician has faced Valencia at the Mestalla on five occasions across his lifetime. In those five matches, he has managed four victories while one ended in a draw. The sole draw came in the Copa Del Rey during his first stint at Real Madrid. As for the four wins, three of them came during his first spell at the Bernabeu as well, while the other victory came during his time at Chelsea, in the UEFA Champions League. A goalscoing fest in order? What is particularly encouraging about Mourinho’s record at the Mestalla is the way his teams have historically dominated in the final third. Real Madrid have done exceptionally well after the break. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) In those five matches, Mourinho’s teams have scored as many as 17 goals, thus accounting for more than three goals per game while conceding only seven. This is quite a remarkable statistic, which could go in line with Real Madrid’s recent scoring form, as Los Blancos have netted at least three goals in a game in five of their last six matches in all competitions. This is despite the fact that Real Madrid will be still missing out on the services of star forward Vinicius Jr., who continues to his serve his four-match suspension after a red card against Villarreal last month. As for Valencia, they are having a horror season with just nine points in 11 matches and are languishing in relegation places. Therefore, it won’t be surprising to see Real Madrid once again scoring three goals under Mourinho at the Mestalla this weekend.

item.description: BINGHAMTON, NY - MAY 26: Franklin Arias #50 of the Portland Sea Dogs celebrates with teammates after defeating the Binghamton Rumble Ponies at Mirabito Stadium on Tuesday, May 26, 2026 in Binghamton, New York. (Photo by Kylie Richelle/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) As Matt laid out yesterday, there sure are a lot of rumors involving the Red Sox and shortstops, despite the fact that Franklin Arias is a shortstop with nothing left to prove in AAA. So what does that say about how the Sox view Arias? Maybe it doesn’t say anything than that they’re doing their due diligence. But here’s what the current dean of the Red Sox beat says about it in his offseason preview piece: “Some in the organization view Arias as almost untouchable. In a poor positional free agent class, however, the Sox are unlikely to keep Arias off-limits in trade talks, but they’d only consider dealing him for a star with multiple years of control.” (Alex Speier, Boston Globe) Meanwhile, another Red Sox beat reporter thinks a big trade isn’t that likely this offseason. “Breslow has gone down the trade road a lot in his three previous offseasons as chief baseball officer. With the prospect haul that was sent to the Orioles for Adley Rutschman, this could be the year free agency is the option Breslow explores the most. Randy Arozarena, to me, would be the perfect fit in the middle of the batting order.” (Ian Browne, MLB.com) Amidst the relatively disappointing start of the “Big Three Era” (remember when it was briefly the “Big Four”?) it’s understandable that many fans harbor some scepticism about prospects like Arias. item.description: Aug 23, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) reacts while warming up prior to a game against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Caitlin Clark has become the face of the WNBA, and the Indiana Fever have become one of the league’s most popular teams because of her. But WNBA legend Angel McCoughtry thinks Clark’s teammate Kelsey Mitchell isn’t getting nearly enough credit. Appearing on the Get To The Point podcast with Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer, McCoughtry argued that looks play a bigger role in WNBA marketing than they do in other sports. She pointed to Mitchell as an example, saying that the Fever’s “best player” is barely recognized by fans. Mitchell’s Big Season Mitchell put together a terrific season for the Fever in 2026. She led the team in scoring, averaging 24.7 points per game, while Clark averaged 22.3 points per game. Mitchell has also been one of Indiana’s most consistent players in recent years, earning All-Star honors and serving as the Fever’s top scoring threat alongside Clark. Still, Clark is the one who draws the crowds and the endorsements. Her arrival turned the Fever into a national draw, and she has become one of the most marketable athletes in sports. ‘Looks play a big part’ McCoughtry, a five-time WNBA All-Star, said that she noticed the gap in attention firsthand. “In the NFL and NBA, if you’re good, you’re good. In the WNBA, if you look pretty… You might not be the best player…” McCoughtry said. “I went to a conference, and everybody loved Indiana. They love Caitlin Clark. I said, ‘How many of you know Kelsey Mitchell?’ None of them raised their hand. She’s the best player on the team,” McCoughtry said, on the podcast . “The leading scorer on that team. Only 100k. She don’t have a million followers.” Owens jumped in to ask if McCoughtry was suggesting that Clark is pretty. She declined to say that she was, but she then brought up Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, pointing out that she has an Adidas shoe deal despite averaging “nine points per game.” Cunningham actually averaged 7.9 points per game this season. McCoughtry said that there are other girls that are “balling” that don’t have similar deals. “Not the best player you’ve ever seen, but she’s getting the brand endorsements,” McCoughtry said. “In the woman’s game, is it really about how good you are or the visibility – how pretty you are?” “Yes, looks play a part. They play a big part,” McCoughtry said. Spencer went on to bring up other examples like Anna Kournikova and Michelle Wei, who weren’t the most successful in their sport but received brand sponsorships, potentially because of their looks. Jackson’s five-year deal included a no-trade clause, meaning that Baltimore needs his explicit approval to move him to another club. The franchise also can’t use the franchise tag on him in 2028 when he expires. That gives Jackson, who doesn’t have an official agent, complete leverage over the situation. Many in sports media and around the National Football League have speculated that the two-time NFL MVP and the storied franchise could potentially part ways after the 2026 season. However, that doesn’t seem to be the plan. Ahead of Baltimore’s Week 8 Thursday Night Football matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Amazon Prime Video that the Ravens are willing to make Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history. When the Kansas City Chiefs reworked the Patrick Mahomes contract in June, the agreement added two years to his contract and made the average annual value a record-setting $64 million. Mahomes and Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott ($60 million AAV) are the only NFL players making $60-plus million per season. Ahead of his age-30 season, it stands to reason that Jackson would be looking for another five-year contract. Baltimore could tack four years onto his current deal, potentially at $65 million per season. It would make him the highest-paid player in NFL history, keep him under contract through his age-35 season and likely allow him to spend his entire career in a Ravens uniform. item.title: Tennessee’s key to beating Kentucky? Don’t beat yourself
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 12: Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel talks with a referee during the college football game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on September 12th, 2026 at Bobby Dodd Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tennessee saw a golden opportunity to give themselves a cushion for the rest of the season two weeks ago in Columbia slip through their fingertips. The Volunteers found a way to lose against South Carolina as the mistakes finally caught up with them late. Tennessee was penalized 12 times for 90 yards against the Gamecocks, famously taking three passing touchdowns from George MacIntyre off the board. The penalties have been a theme for Tennessee ever since Josh Heupel arrived in Knoxville. Heupel’s Tennessee teams have finished outside of the top 100 overall in penalties in four of his five seasons. 2026 has been no different. The Volunteers rank 100th in FBS with 61 penalties on the year. They’re 91st in penalty yards, checking in with 62.12 yards surrendered per game. Tennessee’s opponent this week, Kentucky, is 17th in the same statistic. That’s been a theme for Kentucky all season long — playing clean and taking advantage of opportunities. It’s something that quarterback Kenny Minchey can hang his hat on this year, throwing 14 touchdowns against just one interception. Kentucky has a turnover margin of +13 for the season. Tennessee is +3 in that category for the season. The Volunteers have turned the ball over 11 times on the season, with an opportunistic, aggressive defense propping up their overall margin. Kentucky has turned the ball over just five times all season. “Playing a really good football team that is playing extremely well together,” Josh Heupel said of Kentucky. “You look at their ability to win multiple ways, finish games. Turnover margin, they’ve been elite. One of the least-penalized teams in the league, playing really smart all three phases, so it’ll be a great test.” With an inexperienced quarterback making just his fourth start, keeping things on schedule is a must. The little things — the 3rd and 3 that turns into 3rd and 8 — those are the things that Tennessee really can’t afford down the homestretch, starting on Saturday night. The Volunteers are playing a defensive, ball-control brand this season, and that brand really needs clean football to be successful. We’ll see if Tennessee can clean things up against Kentucky on Saturday. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN.

item.title: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan
item.description: Christian Pulisic’s New Deal Forever Links His Legacy to AC Milan Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract that will keep him at AC Milan until 2031. It is a well-deserved renewal and a career-defining moment for the American winger. Christian Pulisic is staying put at AC Milan . The 28-year-old American winger will remain under contract with the Rossoneri until June 2031, earning a pay rise to €6.5 million net per year, with the figure potentially reaching €10 million if he achieves certain objectives. However you look at it, Pulisic is now one of AC Milan’s highest-paid players and among the top earners in Serie A , alongside Lautaro Martínez , Nicolò Barella, Kevin De Bruyne , and Kenan Yıldız . All of this comes on the heels of Gerry Cardinale, founder and managing partner of RedBird Capital Partners and owner of AC Milan since August 2022, telling CBS Sports: “We have a connection. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to find our way and understand Italy. He’s Captain America, but he’s also my franchise player.” That is an important milestone for an American playing in Europe, particularly one who has already represented three major clubs. Today, Pulisic can look in the mirror and know that his career will be defined by his time at AC Milan, much like Clint Dempsey’s was defined by Fulham or Tim Howard’s by Everton . Pulisic is a Rossoneri player, and for American soccer, that is a remarkable achievement. Pulisic’s Numbers: Not Just Impressive, But a Benchmark The tale of the tape for Pulisic at AC Milan deserves a standing ovation at the San Siro : 45 goals and 28 assists in 144 games. He has also scored four goals against Inter in all competitions, which puts him ahead of Milan legends including Marco van Basten, George Weah, and Ronaldinho . At the UEFA Champions League level, Pulisic has scored five goals, one of which was an Olimpico against Club Brugge . His longest scoring streak has been four consecutive games, a run that included goals against Venezia , Inter and Lecce in Serie A, as well as a Champions League goal against Liverpool . With 45 goals to his name, his tally in Rossoneri stripes surpasses those of Oliver Bierhoff, Robinho, Ronaldinho, Andrea Pirlo , Stephan El Shaarawy, Roberto Donadoni, and Roberto Baggio . The only blemish on Pulisic’s statistics at Milan has been the lack of silverware, with the American having won just one Supercoppa Italiana during his four seasons at the club. That has not been entirely his fault, as Milan have gone through a huge coaching carousel during that period while struggling to find their identity and establish consistency. With Pulisic’s contract approaching its expiration before the renewal, one of the main talking points in Italy was that he could go down as a very good player whose time at the club would ultimately be remembered more for turmoil than success. item.description: Preview: Scott Parker prepares for second game in charge as West Ham travel to Blackburn After a stunning second-half comeback against Cardiff City midweek, West Ham travel to Lancashire to face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Brian Robinson Jr. #15 of the Atlanta Falcons carries the ball against the Carolina Panthers for a first down during the second quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) Getty The Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons are in Madrid, Spain, for what should be a memorable international showdown on Sunday. Ahead of the matchup, which will kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET for viewers in the United States, the Falcons made a sudden change to their injury report. Falcons Rule Out Running Back vs Bengals After listing him as questionable entering Friday morning, the Falcons have officially changed their injury report and ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr. for Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury. This will mark his third consecutive game on the sidelines. Via ESPN’s Adam Schefter: “F alcons ruled out RB Brian Robinson Jr . for Sunday’s game in Madrid against the Bengals due to a hamstring injury.” Falcons ruled out RB Brian Robinson Jr. for Sunday’s game in Madrid against the Bengals due to a hamstring injury. https://t.co/NDIAdtS66M — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 6, 2026 Robinson Jr. has played an important role in the Falcons’ offense this season, often giving starter Bijan Robinson Jr. a break and taking some of the workload off his shoulders. Without Robinson Jr. over the last two games, Atlanta’s other running backs, primarily Khalil Herbert, have produced little to nothing. Robinson Jr.’s 2026 Season With Falcons Robinson Jr. is in his fifth NFL season and first with the Falcons. He has played in six games this year. He has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 4.0 yards per carry. That’s solid production for a backup running back who rarely gets opportunities because Bijan handles most of the workload. Robinson Jr. spent the first three years of his career with the Washington Commanders after a stellar collegiate career at Alabama. At one point, he appeared poised to become Washington’s featured running back. However, he was traded to the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, where he saw limited carries behind Christian McCaffrey.
